title: Dual Shell-like Magnetic Clusters Containing NiII and LnIII (Ln = La, Pr, and Nd) Ions

synthesis.procedure: Ni(NO3)2 hydrate, La(NO3)3·6H2O, and iminodiacetic acid were mixed in deionized water. Aqueous NaOH adjusted the pH to approximately 4. The solution was sealed in a 25-mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel container and heated at 180 °C for 100 h under autogenous pressure. It was cooled at 3 °C h−1 to 100 °C, held for 16 h, then cooled at the same rate to room temperature. Insoluble residue was filtered off; evaporation of the blue filtrate at room temperature gave dark-blue crystals after three months.

properties.summary: Magnetic susceptibility indicates predominantly ferromagnetic coupling and a high-spin ground state; the low-temperature decrease was attributed possibly to intercluster antiferromagnetic interactions and zero-field splitting.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: An outer Ni30 icosidodecahedral shell encloses an inner La20 dodecahedral shell.

synthesis.procedure: The procedure reported for 1 was used with praseodymium(III) nitrate replacing lanthanum(III) nitrate: nickel nitrate hydrate, praseodymium nitrate, and iminodiacetic acid were mixed in 15 mL deionized water, adjusted to approximately pH 4 with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH, and hydrothermally treated in a sealed 25-mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel container at 180 °C for 100 h. The mixture was cooled to 100 °C at 3 °C h−1, held for 16 h, and cooled to room temperature; the filtrate was allowed to evaporate. Block-shaped green crystals were obtained.

synthesis.procedure: The procedure reported for 1 was followed, except that 2.00 mmol rather than 1.00 mmol of lanthanum(III) nitrate was used. Nickel nitrate hydrate, lanthanum nitrate hexahydrate, and iminodiacetic acid were mixed in 15 mL deionized water, adjusted to approximately pH 4 with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH, and heated in a sealed 25-mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel container at 180 °C for 100 h under autogenous pressure. The mixture was cooled to 100 °C at 3 °C h−1, held for 16 h, then cooled to room temperature. After filtration and evaporation of the filtrate, block-shaped blue crystals were isolated.
